grand_strategy.reading:
Portugal runs the strategy of a small Atlantic state that makes itself useful to
every large power around it and commits to none beyond what the treaties force.
Its anchors are three - the EU (money and a Portuguese chair of the European
Council), NATO and the United States (Lajes), and the Lusophone world (Brazil,
Angola, the CPLP) - and its method is conditionality: base access on conditions,
Palestine recognised only with a group, the F-35 kept open, Chinese capital welcomed
but not endorsed. This works while the anchors do not collide. In 2026 they began to:
the Iran war put Lajes between Washington and the Spanish line, the F-16 replacement
asks it to choose between Lockheed and a European hedge it cannot yet pay for, and
the CPLP is splitting over Equatorial Guinea. At home the cost shows in a minority
government, a president of the other party who speaks more sharply than the foreign
minister, and Chega, which polls first on the one issue (immigration) where the
Lusophone strategy and the electorate pull apart. Expect Lisbon to stay the quietest
reliable ally until Washington asks for something it cannot dress in conditions.

grand_strategy.reading:
The State of Palestine is a state whose government cannot protect its people, finance itself or even hold an election, and it knows it: its grand strategy is the strategy of staying in
the picture. Everything Ramallah does is a bet that the Palestinian question will be settled by others and that whoever is still standing, with a flag, a seat at the UN and a legal
personality, will be handed what is left. That produces the Luttwak pattern in its sharpest form: the means that keep the Authority alive (coordination with Israel, endorsement of the
Trump plan, reform pledges to donors, a managed succession) are the same that drain its credibility with Palestinians, while the means that raise its standing abroad (157 recognitions, the
ICJ opinion, the ICC) are punished with the loss of money and travel. In 2025-26 the pressure came from three sides at once: Israel's fiscal strangulation and settlement drive (UN: 'the PA
is at the brink of collapse'), a US-designed Gaza order that includes technocrats but not the Authority, and Hamas, which is losing public support (24%) but not its arms. The Western wave of
recognition in September 2025 and the settlement-goods bans of 2026 are real, but they give the Authority diplomatic oxygen, not territory or revenue. Two signals that are not rows: Abbas telling
the UN on 24 Sep 2026 that elections were on and postponing them sixteen days later, and the US ban that again kept him out of New York. With Israeli elections on 27 Oct 2026, the PA's real
question is whether a new government in Jerusalem would unfreeze the clearance revenues or whether the money, not the flag, decides its survival.

grand_strategy.reading:
Qatar runs the strategy of a rich micro-state that has no army to match its
neighbours and therefore sells services in exchange for protection: gas to the
world, mediation to the great powers, money to the weak, and a base to
Washington. The strategy worked for thirty years because the bill was paid in
influence rather than force; since June 2025 the bill has come due. Israel
struck its capital with the United States on notice, Iran fired at it three
times and took out a sixth of its LNG capacity, and Hormuz showed that the whole
franchise exits through a single strait that the aggressor controls. The reply
is a reconstruction of deterrence: a written US guarantee (EO 14353, a
presidential order rather than a treaty), a Turkish tie, air defence that has
now shot down aircraft, and a vocabulary of Gulf self-sufficiency that Doha
shares with Abu Dhabi. Luttwak's pattern is the paradoxical one: each asset that
buys security (Al Udeid, Hamas as interlocutor, Iran as neighbour, LNG as
leverage) is the one that draws the fire. Two signals that are not rows: Qatar
refused in March 2026 to lead US-Iran mediation so that attacking it would not
earn Tehran better terms, and returned to the table by August; and Doha is
spending its mediation capital on the places where it still has leverage
(Gaza, DRC, Ukraine's children, Afghanistan) while the Iranian file belongs to
Pakistan. The next test is whether the written guarantee holds and whether
Hormuz reopens before buyers decide that Qatar is a risk to be hedged.

grand_strategy.reading: Romania is a frontline state with a rear-area politics. Its grand strategy is borrowed security: bind the United States, NATO and the EU to the Black Sea by hosting their bases, buying their arms with their loans and keeping Ukraine and Moldova alive as buffers. The method has worked in hardware (Kogalniceanu, Deveselu, F-35s, SAFE) and fails at the margin Washington controls: the brigade left in October 2025 while Bucharest was offering a base for the Iran operation five months later. What is new in 2026 is that the weak point is internal. The annulled election of 2024 did not remove the sovereigntist vote, a third of Parliament, and the fiscal repair that the EU and the rating agencies demanded took the coalition apart; the country has had a caretaker cabinet since 5 May and a fourth nominee since 5 October, with every agency one step above junk. Neighbours show the same split between kinship and interest: Moldova is kin and a partner, Ukraine is a partner and a dispute over Romanian schools, Hungary is a co-member whose new government (Magyar, April 2026) has restarted the conversation, Serbia is a partner it presses on the Vlachs, Turkey the one NATO ally in the Black Sea with ships and a strategic partnership. China is held at arm's length by law (the 5G rules that exclude Huawei) and, since Dan's remarks on the 2025 strategy, with open caution; Israel is a partner whose war Romania abstained on in 2023 and 2024 and voted for the Palestinian seat in 2026. Read through Luttwak, the danger is that Romania's policy of making itself useful rests on stable government in Bucharest, which is the thing it lacks.

grand_strategy.reading:
Saudi Arabia is a rich state that has become a front-line state without
changing its aim, which is to buy time for an economy that will outlast oil.
Everything in the card is a trade of one scarce thing for another: US
protection against Israeli normalisation, a Pakistani and Turkish guarantee
against dependence on Washington, the UAE's exit from Yemen against a Houthi
front of its own, a wartime oil price against lost volume and market share.
The Luttwakian pattern is that each safeguard creates the next exposure: the
February 2026 war put Iranian missiles on Ras Tanura and Riyadh, the
answers (strikes in Iraq, an offensive in Yemen) brought the Houthis to the
capital's airport, and the hedges (Makkah pact, Pakistani troops) show a
kingdom unsure that the United States will fight for it. The thaw with Abu Dhabi
(July-October 2026) is tactical, since Yemen's south, Sudan and the Horn
remain contested. Signals that are not rows: the postponement, at Riyadh's
request, of the Hormuz talks between Gulf states and Iran in Sept 2026
(Saudi Arabia would rather the US negotiates than the Gulf legitimises
Iranian control of the strait); Egypt declining the Makkah pact while saying
Gulf security is its own; and the fiscal arithmetic that makes the 2026 deficit look
better only because the war lifts the price. Open gaps in this pass: the
OIC and Arab League as instruments, Afghanistan, Jordan, Kuwait, Oman, the
Horn beyond commentary, and an official Saudi source for the Houthi truce
breakdown (reports date the renewed fighting from June or July 2026).

grand_strategy.reading:
Serbia runs a hedging strategy with one fixed point - Kosovo - and everything else
negotiable. In Luttwak's terms the paradox is structural: the instrument that
protects the fixed point (Russian and Chinese cover at the UN) is the one that
blocks the declared strategic goal (EU membership), and the "neutrality" that
justifies the hedge is financed by the side the hedge is meant to keep at a
distance. Through 2025-26 the hedge stopped paying: the US sanctioned NIS, Russia
refused a long-term gas contract and accused Belgrade over ammunition, the EU
froze funds and talks after the Mladić funeral. Two signals worth watching that
are not rows: Vučić did not attend the 2026 Moscow parade, and in May 2026 Serbia
held its first-ever exercise with NATO on its own soil. The 25 Oct 2026 election
decides whether the strategy has an author at all.

grand_strategy.reading:
Republika Srpska is an entity of a state that it works to hollow out, run by a
party that kept the entity three times in a year in which its leader lost his
office. Its grand strategy is the strategy of a sub-state actor whose
patron needs it loud but not detached: Belgrade wants a Republika Srpska strong
enough to hold Bosnia hostage to the Serbian cause and keep the Sarajevo
state weak, but not so detached that Serbia must either own a secession or
disown a kin. That makes the entity's best move the threat, not the act - and
here Luttwak's paradoxical logic bites hardest. Each time Banja Luka has
crossed the line (the laws of 27 Feb 2025) the state's institutions have
reacted (court annulment, EUFOR reserve troops, entry bans, the High
Representative's funding cut), and those institutions came out stronger and
better tested than before; the repeal of 18 Oct 2025 was a retreat that
Washington rewarded within eleven days. The lesson Banja Luka drew is not
restraint but timing: escalate, absorb, retreat for a price, and let paid
lobbyists and a weaker OHR (Schmidt out in May 2026, an acting High
Representative from 1 July) do the rest.

Signals that are not rows. The plea agreement and the pardon: no source reached
shows a plea agreement between Dodik and the State Prosecutor's Office, and
the prison term was converted into a fine of about EUR 18,660 on 12 Aug 2025
at the defence's request, the six-year ban untouched; in October 2026
Bosnian media discuss whether the state Presidency could pardon him, which
would need all three members and the prior opinion of the State Court - a
debate, not an act. Orban's defeat in April 2026 removes the entity's best
door in the EU, and no source on the new Hungarian government's line toward
Banja Luka was found. The entity's two stable patrons are therefore
Belgrade (kin, bounded) and Moscow (kin, expensive); its transactional ones
are Washington, Budapest, Jerusalem, Ankara and Beijing, none of which has a
treaty with it.

grand_strategy.reading:
Slovakia is the case of a small, trade-dependent member state that uses
the rules of the club it belongs to as its main instrument against the
club. Fico has no army to speak of, no oil, and an export economy
wired into German supply chains; what he has is unanimity. The 2023-26
pattern is therefore linkage: a veto (the 18th and 20th sanctions
packages, Ukraine's loan, the accession clusters) is held until a
concrete good is released - gas guarantees, Druzhba oil, a hearing. That
is Luttwak's paradoxical logic in a small space: the weaker the state,
the more it relies on the one resource, procedure, that its partners
cannot take away without breaking their own rules. But the lever
consumes itself. Hungary under Orban was the other half of the veto
axis; after Magyar's win in April 2026 Bratislava is alone, the
Parliament has asked for conditionality, and the Visegrad revival is
being run by Tusk, Babis and Magyar, not by Fico. Two signals that are
not rows: Fico took the Moscow trip again in May 2026 after having
been shot in 2024 and after a year of mass protest, which shows that
the trips are a message to a domestic electorate and not a
diplomatic programme (OSW and others make this reading of the
American hardware too); and on 18 Sep 2026 he said he would not
be 'part of any military conflict because of Article 5' - a statement
that, if believed, hollows out the alliance whose F-16s he is flying.
The coalition crisis of September 2026 may end the story before the
2027 election: the structural question is whether his successor,
whoever it is, will inherit a state that has learned to veto or one
that has learned to be vetoed.

Slovenia is a small, rich, open economy whose strategy is to stay inside every
club (EU, euro, Schengen, NATO) and to spend as little as possible on anything
that is not membership. Its distinctive feature in 2022-26 is that the content
of foreign policy swings with the government while the anchors do not move:
Golob's Slovenia used the Security Council seat to be the EU's most outspoken
critic of Israel; Janša's Slovenia, since June 2026, pays its dues to NATO,
courts Trump and reopens to Israel. One signal that is not a row: Israel's
announced embassy in Ljubljana, the visible reward for the reversal.

advocacy, China, Italy, Trieste and Koper, tariffs and the Hungarian media loan.

grand_strategy.reading: Sweden after 2022 runs the strategy of a small, rich, technologically capable state that has given up the protection of neutrality for the protection of numbers, and is spending to make the swap pay. The organising idea is the Baltic as a NATO lake: Finland, Poland and Denmark are treated as one theatre, the Gripen, the A26 and the CV90 are the instruments of alignment as much as of defence, and the United States is kept inside the system by treaty (the DCA) while Europe is built up for the day it steps back. The Luttwakian pattern is that every step that raises Sweden's value to the alliance also raises its exposure and its bills (the front-line host, the donated Gripens, the loans behind 3.5%), and that the bargains that bought the membership (Turkey, Hungary) taught others that a veto has a price. Two signals are not rows. First, the 13 September 2026 vote ended the Tidö era without producing a successor: the next government will probably keep NATO, Ukraine and the 3.5% target (all large Riksdag majorities) but will change the Israel line and perhaps the EU budget posture, so the card's stability is higher on security than on foreign economic policy. Second, the brief's 'Ukraine 100-year partnership' is not in the record: Sweden's agreement with Ukraine is a ten-year security agreement of May 2024; a 100-year format belongs to the United Kingdom. grand_strategy.reading:
Syria under Ahmed al-Sharaa runs the grand strategy of a victorious insurgency
that has to become a state before its patrons lose patience. The rank order of the
objectives is the order of the dangers: first the monopoly of force (the SDF
deal, Suwayda, the coast), then legitimacy (delistings, sanctions relief, Caesar
repeal), then money. The method is multi-alignment at the leader level, with no
patron allowed to own the state: Turkey for the army, the Gulf for the cash,
Washington for the permission to trade, Russia kept only as a training partner,
Iran expelled. The Luttwak pattern is that each move that builds the state
also invites an outsider into it: the Turkish umbrella draws the Israeli strike,
the conquest of the east takes away the American cover, the pressure on
minorities supplies the conditions that Western money carries. Signals that are
not rows: the Syrian army's deployment to the Lebanese border in March 2026,
al-Sharaa's refusal to attend the 2025 Baghdad summit, and Egypt's refusal of a
Syrian ambassador. Open question for the next review: whether the 25 Aug SDF
dissolution survives its first test in Hasakah and Kobani, and whether an
Israeli security agreement is signed or the south settles into a frozen
occupation. Not read in this pass: Crisis Group and Carnegie analyses of 2026
(the search budget ran out), so grades on Israel, Russia and China rest on press
and official statements.

Riyadh and Islamabad, and offers itself as the venue and mediator that every
side needs. The currency is indispensability, and it works because nobody can
afford to push Ankara out. Luttwak's pattern appears at each seam: the S-400 that
proved autonomy cost the F-35; the victory in Syria draws Israeli bombs on its
airbase; the Blue Homeland decrees imperil the customs union; the boycott of
Israel closes the Gaza seat. Underneath sits regime security. The two things the
leadership most needs in 2026 - the end of the PKK war (Law 7595, the SDF's
dissolution) and a path to keep power (the İmamoğlu trial) - are domestic
before they are foreign, and they set the tone of the external line: a
'Terror-Free Türkiye' that justifies Syrian and Iraqi policy, and a Western
reconciliation (Trump's promise of sanctions relief and the F-35) pursued
without conditions on rule of law. Signals that are not rows: Ankara has not
joined Western sanctions on Russia and cut Russian crude only after Trump's
appeal of Sept 2025; Washington's envoy to Syria is also its ambassador in
Ankara, which makes Turkey the channel for US policy in Damascus. The open
questions for the next quarter are whether Trump's promise becomes a legal
instrument, whether the Blue Homeland law passes in October, and whether the
Israel-Turkey deconfliction mechanism in Syria is built before the next strike.

grand_strategy.reading:
Ukraine runs a grand strategy of the weaker party that must make itself
indispensable to stronger ones: it cannot win the war outright, cannot
afford to lose it, and has to keep three patrons (the EU, the UK-led
coalition, the United States) paying while it negotiates with an adversary
whose price is its statehood. At the tactical level it is holding (the
front is slow in 2026, drones and strikes compensate for men), at the
theatre level it is trading minerals, drones and the promise of a rebuilt
country for money and guarantees, and at the grand-strategic level it is
betting that the road to the EU gives it an anchor that no ceasefire can
cancel. Luttwak's reversal is everywhere: the same logic that keeps the
patrons engaged (usefulness, visible strength, deep strikes, a national
story told in battle) irritates the neighbours whose vetoes decide the
anchor, from Fico's pipeline to Warsaw's history. 2026 is also the year the
centre of the question moved from the front to the table: talks opened
in Abu Dhabi in January, were frozen by the Iran war in March, and resumed
with the Miami round of 9-10 October, while the Kremlin still demands the
Donbas. Two signals that are not rows: the new Hungarian government's
shift from veto to conditions (Magyar, since May) and the Ankara
summit's quiet re-labelling of Ukraine as a contributor to Euro-Atlantic
security. Open question for the next review: whether the 15 Oct European
Council and the Miami outcome change the guarantee from a text to a force.

grand_strategy.reading: The Holy See has no army and no military allies, so its grand strategy is diplomatic and moral: keep 184 states talking to it, keep the Church alive where it is restricted, and make the pope's voice count in wars it cannot stop. Under Leo XIV, elected on 8 May 2025 as the first American-born pope, the line continues Francis but is sharper on migration and Gaza, and it accepts cooler relations with Washington as the price. The weak points are money (a structural deficit covered by Peter's Pence) and China, where the 2018 deal is the main file and the clearest case of a channel kept open at the cost of its text. Recognition is the currency it trades: Taiwan (one of the few states with relations with the Republic of China), Palestine since 2015, and the Lebanon and Turkey trip of late 2025 as a way to speak to Middle East Christians. Non-events to watch: no US visit was planned for 2026, and the Ukraine talks offer in Vatican City has not been accepted by Moscow.

grand_strategy.reading:
Kosovo runs the strategy of a state that exists on the ground and not yet in
law: every move is a bid to turn effective control into recognised status, and
the only currencies it has are loyalty and usefulness to the West. That
produces the central Luttwakian pattern: the actions that prove statehood
(mayors in the north, the army, rail stations, the war-memory law) are the
ones that cost it the patrons who could confer it, while the actions that would
please the patrons (the Community of Serb-majority Municipalities, Serbian
return to the judiciary) are those it fears would hollow out statehood from
within. Since 2025 the pressure has eased on one flank (EU measures lifted in
March 2026, institutions completed in September-October) and tightened on
another (KFOR shrinking, a cooler Washington, the Specialist Chambers
verdicts). Two signals that are not rows: the US launched a strategic dialogue with
Belgrade on 17 July 2026 although Kosovo had joined the Board of Peace and
pledged troops to Gaza, and the 6 Oct law on the Hague court was passed under
street pressure, not diplomatic calculation. With
the 25 Oct Serbian election ahead, Pristina's real question is whether the
stalled Ohrid road can be re-opened by a new government in Belgrade.

grand_strategy.reading:
The internationally recognised government of Yemen is a state held up from outside: legal
seat at the UN, salaries and grants from Riyadh, air power largely Saudi, and most of its people
beyond its writ. Its grand strategy is therefore less a plan than a position in a Saudi
plan, and Luttwak's levels diverge sharply. At the theatre level the goal is the
Houthis' defeat (the PLC's own word is the 'decisive phase', 4 Oct 2026); at the
grand-strategic level the goal is to remain the party Riyadh must keep, against a
Houthi movement that Riyadh has negotiated with since 2022 and against an Emirati
network it destroyed in January 2026. The 2026 sequence is the paradox of the card:
the elimination of the STC bought Saudi control of the south and left the camp
without its best money and units, then the coast fell within a week; the Iran war
turned the Bab al-Mandab into a bargaining chip, so that the contest over Yemen's
coast is settled in Tehran, Riyadh, Washington and Muscat as much as in Taiz and
Mokha. What decides the next year is Saudi stamina and Saudi pain: the government
needs the offensive to continue and cannot control the price Riyadh pays. Signals
that are not rows: the Houthis' own account of their aims (Sanaa-based media only,
not researched); the Southern movement after the STC's formal dissolution, which
appears in the sources only as protest and bombings; the UAE's silence on Yemen
since January except for condemning the strikes on Saudi airports.

AFG.note: Pakistan was the Taliban's patron and sanctuary; since 9 Oct 2025 (first Pakistani strike on Kabul) it is the Emirate's main military enemy: border war in October 2025, Doha/Istanbul ceasefire talks that failed, 'open war' declared by Khawaja Asif on 26-27 Feb 2026 with strikes on Kabul and Kandahar, a truce from 18 Mar, talks in Urumqi in April, new strikes on 24 Sep 2026; borders mostly closed since 12 Oct 2025; over 2.4 million Afghans returned from Pakistan since 2023. Zelin (WINEP, Aug 2026) says Pakistan went 'from patron to adversary' - a source that uses the stronger word. Adversary test: the grade stays rival because neither side's declared aim is the other's disappearance. Islamabad says borders reopen on 'decisive and verifiable action' against the TTP and keeps attending China-, Qatar-, Turkey- and Saudi-mediated talks; Kabul says it is 'open to talks', sends delegations, and treats the TTP as Pakistan's internal affair. Asif's 'obliterate' and 'open war' lines and the Taliban's claim that Pakistan backs anti-Taliban fronts are the argument for adversary and are the reason the trend is cooling and the confidence C; if Pakistan states a regime-change aim or Kabul seeks Pakistani territory, regrade. Bond - grievance: the TTP sanctuary, deportations, the Durand Line, the trade closures. Asymmetric pairing with PAK's own side is expected to differ (Islamabad is likely to grade Kabul adversary).

BGD.note: Why not rival: the BNP government wants the relationship repaired (Rahman's adviser asked for a 'complete reset', the foreign minister went to New Delhi on 7-8 Apr 2026, Dhaka reopened visas for Indians within three days of taking office and asks for more diesel and fertiliser), and Bangladesh cannot do without Indian power (15.6% of supply in 2025), fuel, transit and water. Why not partner: Dhaka resists any alignment ('Bangladesh First', sovereign equality), holds Hasina's extradition (death sentence of 17 Nov 2025; India 'examining' the request in April, July and August 2026) as the price of Rahman's first visit, protests the BSF's border killings (at least 34 in the first 11 months of the interim government) and the pushbacks, and read India's 2025 import restrictions (about USD 770m of trade) as coercion. Cooling since 5 Aug 2026 (Hasina's virtual press conference; the India trip put on hold; BRICS invitation declined 10 Sep). No source uses the exact label; Al Jazeera's reading ('there is no alternative' to dialogue; initial warmth gave way to nationalist rhetoric on both sides) and WPR's ('mild to severe turbulence') are the closest, so the grade is our structural reading (C). Indian-side commentary and ORF are flagged as the Indian view. Bond - grievance: 1971 gratitude has been replaced by a decade of perceived Indian patronage of the Hasina regime, the Ganges and Teesta waters and border deaths.

DEU.note: Germany's 2023 National Security Strategy calls Russia the greatest threat to peace in the Euro-Atlantic area for the foreseeable future, Pistorius puts a possible Russian attack on NATO at 2029 or earlier, and the federal prosecutor has charged sabotage and espionage plots in 2025-26 (three men over rail sabotage, a Kazakh national in Berlin; 165+ suspected incidents in 2026 per SZ). Not 'adversary': the same strategy says Germany and NATO do not seek hostility or confrontation, and Berlin's declared aim is deterrence and Ukraine's survival, not Russia's defeat or the end of its regime (compare Poland's 'adversary' and the Czech and Croatian 'rival'). No source uses the word 'rival': the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C), one step from adversary. Bond - grievance: the war and the Nord Stream dependence Berlin now regrets.

DNK.note: NATO treaty ally since 1949, host of Pituffik and of US forces under the 2023 Defence Cooperation Agreement (approved 94-11, June 2025), buyer of 43 F-35s - and the target of Trump's claim to Greenland since December 2024 (tariff threat 6 Jan 2025, Vance at Pituffik 28 Mar 2025, envoy Landry Dec 2025, 10% tariff threat on 17 Jan 2026, invasion not ruled out until Davos on 21 Jan). Foreign Minister Rasmussen: a 'fundamental disagreement' that the two sides 'agree to disagree' on, while having said after Vance's visit (March 2025) that he 'still considers' the US a close ally. The 22 Sep 2026 trilateral agreement ends the crisis on paper but the readings differ (Trump: 'permanent control'; Frederiksen: sovereignty recognised) and Trump repeated the claim at Ankara in July. Grade follows the structure: a treaty ally under open friction, per the ontology, not a rival. Trend stable rather than warming because the deal is contested. Bond - grievance: the coercion of 2025-26 is an open wound inside the alliance.

FIN.note: Why rival and not adversary: Finland's own line is that Russia is not an enemy but its actions and breaches of international law are opposed (Valtonen, April 2025), and the declared strategy is to support Ukraine, weaken Russia through sanctions and strengthen defence - deterrence and containment, not an aim of Russia's defeat or regime. Yet the Government Defence Report (Dec 2024) calls Russia a long-term threat that will outlast the war, Supo names it the main threat, the eastern border has been shut since December 2023, Russia closed five rail crossings on 1 Jul 2026, and Peskov says Finland and Sweden 'reduced relations to zero'. Stubb (31 Mar 2025) says Finns must prepare mentally for an eventual thaw, so the door is not closed. Bond - grievance: Winter War memory and the 1,340 km border, now sharpened by hybrid pressure (instrumentalised migration, GNSS jamming, cable incidents). Our reading of the grade is C-level on the word itself; the structure is documented by tier 1 sources.

Friction is minimal and is aimed at members (US tariffs) rather than at the alliance. Bond - affinity: Finns chose membership after seventy years of non-alignment; support is above 70%.

Reluctant ally because the dependency (Trident, F-35A, GPS and intelligence) keeps the UK aligned against its present preference. Bond - affinity: language, history, intelligence and nuclear kinship; no grievance.

Friction is sharp and rising: Serbian diplomat expulsions and reciprocal moves (Nov 2023), Belgrade's ambassador recalled after the 18 Mar 2025 Tirana declaration, Vucic's 'greatest threat' line (Munich 2026), Plenkovic writing to NATO about Serbia's CM-400AKG missiles (Mar 2026), Milanovic cancelling the Brdo-Brijuni summit (30 Mar 2026), 1,725 missing persons with no archive cooperation. Croatia is also the sole crude route for Serbia (JANAF), which makes the pair interdependent. Bond - grievance: the 1991-95 war, Vukovar and Jasenovac as memory.

HUN.note: Member since 2004, so the 'partner' grade of non-members does not apply; the co-member rule gives reluctant_ally while friction remains. Sixteen years of vetoes and Article 7 ended with the 12 Apr 2026 election (Tisza 53%, 138 of 199 seats; 'the Hungarian people have said yes to Europe'). The Commission proposed on 23 Sep 2026 to release EUR 4.2bn of the funds frozen since 2022 and the Council meets on 13 Oct; EUR 3.5bn is still blocked over the child-protection, academic-freedom and asylum files, and Hungary's court case against the EU's Russian gas ban and the migration-pact fight show the friction is not over. Bond affinity: a government that wants to be inside, not a rebel.

HUN.note: NATO ally, so not 'partner'. Washington was Orban's patron: Vance campaigned for him days before the vote, Trump gave him a one-year waiver on Russian oil and gas sanctions and an open-ended one for Paks II in Nov 2025 against US LNG and nuclear-fuel purchases. After the vote Trump called Magyar 'a good man' and the US embassy promised close cooperation, but no White House invitation is reported, a pro-Fidesz outlet describes a missed handshake at the Ankara summit, and the waiver lapses on 21 Nov 2026 with Budapest asking for an extension. The 'cooling' is a reading of lost patronage, not a US act (confidence C). Bond affinity: the Biden-era freeze is over and migration politics still overlaps.

HUN.note: Treaty-based strategic partnership (2021) with a defence agreement (2023, implementing agreement 2025) that Belgrade reads as an alliance and Telex calls 'a far cry from' one; Serbia grades Hungary 'ally'. Cooling because the personal patron is gone. Bond affinity: Vojvodina's minority and the shared sovereigntist camp.

IND.note: The ontology's adversary test: does New Delhi seek the end of the Pakistani state or its regime? The record says no. After the Pahalgam attack (22 Apr 2025, 26 killed, claimed by TRF, which India calls a Lashkar-e-Taiba front) India struck nine 'terrorist sites' in Operation Sindoor on 7 May 2025, fought four days of missile, drone and artillery exchanges, and then accepted a ceasefire agreed between the two DGMOs on 10 May; it targets terror infrastructure and the army's sponsorship of it, calls the new line 'if Pakistan fires, we fire', and keeps the Pakistani state as the counterpart it holds responsible. The Indus Waters Treaty is 'in abeyance' since 23 Apr 2025 'until Pakistan credibly and irrevocably abjures cross-border terrorism' (MEA, 3 Jul 2026) - leverage with a stated exit condition, not an end-state. India does claim all of Jammu and Kashmir including Pakistan-held territory, and engagement is now limited to terrorism and PoK. After the Red Fort car bomb in Delhi (10 Nov 2025, 12-15 killed, a Jaish-e-Mohammed link noted by the UN monitoring team in Feb 2026) India did not formally blame Pakistan or retaliate, which shows the threshold is attribution, not each incident. That is a rivalry with a nuclear shadow and an arms race, not a war of existence, so `rival`, not `adversary`; the Pakistani side (Munir's army, the Saudi pact, Chinese kit) reads India as the existential threat, which is why the pair is asymmetric in feeling but not in grade. Mediation is refused (Kashmir is bilateral; India denies the US brokered the ceasefire). Bond - grievance: partition, four wars, Kashmir. Confidence B because the grade is our structural reading of sources that describe the pair as rivals and India's own posture as deterrence.

IND.note: A partner whose year was a stress test. The 2025 US tariffs reached 50% in Aug 2025 (25% 'reciprocal' plus 25% for buying Russian oil) and put ties 'at their lowest in nearly two decades' (Tribune); the 100,000-dollar H-1B fee (19 Sep 2025) hit the pipeline of Indian engineers (Indians were 71% of 2024 approvals). Repair followed: the 10-year Framework for the US-India Major Defence Partnership signed in Kuala Lumpur on 31 Oct 2025, the 2 Feb 2026 deal cutting the rate to 18% in exchange for restricting Russian oil and buying more American goods, the Quad foreign ministers in New Delhi on 26 May 2026. But the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs on 20 Feb 2026, the first-phase trade agreement is still unsigned (Goyal in June: '99 percent' settled), the Quad leaders' summit India was to host has no date, and on 17 Sep 2026 Congress passed an act authorising tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian energy, to which the MEA answered it will 'take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests'. Net direction: neither warming nor cooling, with the US pulling harder on Russian oil than at any time since 2022. Not an ally: no treaty, no basing, India refuses mediation on Pakistan and keeps Russia. Bond - affinity: diaspora, technology, shared China concern.

Partner, not ally: no mutual-defence clause, and India is choosing French Rafale rather than Russian aircraft for its next fighters (see FRA). Trend stable: Moscow is leaning on India more as its own partners shrink, but New Delhi is reducing exposure on arms, not on oil. Bond - affinity: Soviet-era friendship and a shared reading of multipolarity, but no kinship.

IRN.note: Mortal enemies in the ontology's reference sense, and mutual. Israel struck Iran's nuclear and military sites in the twelve-day war (13-24 Jun 2025) and again from 28 Feb 2026 with the US; Netanyahu called on Iranians to overthrow their rulers, while a US official said 'regime change is one of theirs' (Reuters, 4 Mar). Tehran answers with saturation fire on Israeli cities (31 civilians killed in 2026 by Israel's count) and the new leader's pledge of vengeance 'until fully achieved' (12 Mar). Iran's side of the aim is the weaker part of the proof: no source in hand quotes a current Iranian text calling for Israel's destruction, so the grade rests on the war itself, the decapitation strike on Khamenei and the vengeance message; confidence B, not A. Bond - grievance: the Khamenei killing, the 2025 and 2026 wars and Israel's offensive in Lebanon, which Tehran wants in any ceasefire.

IRN.note: Graded adversary, not rival, and this is the least comfortable grade of the card. For: the US and Israel opened the war on 28 Feb 2026 with the declared aim of regime change (Reuters, 4 Mar: 'at the outset, Trump and Netanyahu both said regime change was the goal'), killed Ali Khamenei, kept a naval blockade of Iranian ports from 13 Apr (reinstated 13 Jul) and resumed strikes on 8 Jul; Mojtaba Khamenei's first message demanded that 'all US bases in the region must close' and promised vengeance; Iran fired at Al Udeid in June 2025 and at US-hosting Gulf states from 28 Feb 2026 (6,700+ missiles and drones by 17 May, per the CRS). Against: Hegseth said the operation was not 'a so-called regime-change war', Trump moved to missiles, navy and the bomb, Vance asks for a 'meaningful' cut in enrichment, and the two presidents signed the Pakistan-brokered memorandum of 17 Jun. The atlas reads it as a war between two states each of which would accept the other's defeat, with talks as an instrument of the war, not a thaw. If a settlement on enrichment and Hormuz holds, the right grade becomes rival. Bond - grievance since the 1979 embassy seizure, and now the dead leader.

Luxembourg took part in the EU discussions on the immobilised Russian assets while stating it was not directly affected by the 2024 securities-depository rules. LUX.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded from partner to reluctant_ally - Luxembourg and the United States are NATO treaty co-members, so friction (the Feb 2026 'rupture' trip, tax and Greenland) makes a reluctant ally, never a partner, by the ontology rule. Since is the earliest dated sign of the current posture (Feb 2026 trip), not the start of diplomatic relations (1903, not separately sourced here). Transactional, not aligned by treaty beyond NATO: Luxembourg's Prime Minister travelled to Boston and Ottawa in early February 2026 and the French-language press framed it as a possible 'rupture' with the US, with a push to strengthen other partnerships. The US is a financial and tax partner (no tax-treaty source gathered yet). Greenland: no Luxembourg role found in the sources. Grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C); no source uses the word 'partner' for Luxembourg-US. Bond - none.

LUX.note: Since is the EU immobilisation regulation of 13 Dec 2025 (the current sanctions posture), not the start of diplomatic relations (1891, not separately sourced here). Sanctions and assets rather than enmity: Luxembourg implements EU sanctions and holds Russian central-bank assets through Clearstream and the financial system; the EU regulation of Dec 2025 immobilised them indefinitely, and Luxembourg's exposure is contested (estimates range from EUR 5.5bn in an older Commission figure to about EUR 10bn in a Parliament briefing we could not retrieve). No sourced statement calls Russia a rival; the grade is our reading of the structure. Bond - none; no kinship or grievance.

LVA.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded from adversary to rival for consistency with Estonia and Lithuania; 'adversary' is reserved for actors seeking each other's destruction (Iran-Israel). The Saeima's 'state sponsor of terrorism' declaration and the chargé-level relations are the hardest posture in NATO, but Riga's aim is deterrence and a Russian defeat in Ukraine, not the end of the Russian state. The Latvian state itself uses the vocabulary of the mortal enemy: the State Security Service (VDD) puts Russia's services at the head of the threats to the state and a secondary account of its February 2026 report calls Russia an existential threat; the Saeima declared Russia a state sponsor of terrorism on 11 Aug 2022 (67 votes, none against); relations were cut to charge d'affaires level on 24 Feb 2023; and Latvian soil has seen Russian-directed arson cells (cases of 2023-25), GPS jamming from Kaliningrad, and Russian rail crossings shut from 1 Jul 2026. Adversary rather than rival because the declared Latvian aim is Russia's defeat in Ukraine and the Russian state is named the threat to Latvia's existence, not a competitor. The case against: Riga seeks no change of regime in Moscow, keeps an embassy, and still sold EUR 962.5m of goods to Russia in 2025 (4.9% of exports), so the grade is the harder of two readings (the 'rival' reading is the fallback). Bond - grievance: the 1940 occupation and the Soviet deportations, and more than a third of residents who are not ethnic Latvians, mostly Russian-speaking.

LVA.note: Mirrors Belarus's own card (rival, bond none, C): Latvia closed Silene on 19 Sep 2023 and has kept it shut, stopped nearly 10,000 illegal crossing attempts in the first eight months of 2026 (12,046 in all of 2025), found two tunnels in August 2026, opened a criminal case in mid-July 2026 against Belarusian border officials for moving migrants in state vehicles, and the Interior Ministry proposed on 4 Aug to close Paternieki, the last crossing, as 'hybrid pressure' (the government declined on 5 Aug). The VDD reads Belarusian services as an extension of Russian ones. Rival and not adversary: the aim is to stop a pressure, not to remove the Minsk regime, and Riga keeps one crossing open and EUR 132.5m of exports (0.7%). No source uses the word 'rival': our reading (confidence C). Cooling because 2026 is the heaviest year yet.

LVA.note: NATO Article 5 is the floor and the Latvian government says it has 'no doubt' the US would come to help (Defence Minister Sprud, 23 Apr 2026), while buying six HIMARS and ATACMS munitions (about USD 180m, from 2027). Cooling is on Washington's side, not Riga's: relations between the US and its allies were at a 'historic low' in April 2026, Washington warned Nordic and Baltic buyers of delays to approved weapons, and the Pentagon's posture review left Lithuania and Estonia with rotation gaps in June-July 2026 (no Latvian gap is reported). President Rinkevics said after the Ankara summit (July 2026) that 'contentious rhetoric' will not disappear. Ally and not reluctant_ally because Latvia does not resist the alignment; the friction is the US's reliability. Bond - affinity: the United States never recognised the 1940 annexation.

The one visible friction is the 7 May 2026 incident, when Ukrainian drones diverted by Russian jamming hit the Rezekne oil depot and Kyiv blamed Russian electronic warfare. The EU Treaty's Article 42(7) is the derived floor. Friction: EU funding for Rail Baltica is short (a funding gap of about EUR 10bn across the Baltics) and the Istanbul Convention debate of autumn 2025 split the Silina coalition from the EU's line. Warming because SAFE and Eastern Flank Watch money are now arriving. Bond - affinity: Brussels is read as the second guarantee after NATO.

LVA.note: Latvia and Estonia left China's 16+1 format on 11 Aug 2022 (Lithuania left in May 2021), with Riga saying it would keep 'constructive and pragmatic' relations; the VDD names Chinese services among the risks to national security; and Beijing's support for Russia puts it on the wrong side of the one issue that organises Latvian policy. Rival and not neutral because of the exit and the intelligence flag; not adversary because there is no hostile aim and China is a significant import source (12.6% of electrical machinery imports). No source uses the word 'rival': our reading (confidence C). Bond - none.

MKD.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). Bulgaria is the first obstacle on Skopje's EU path: it has blocked the opening of negotiations since 2020 and, with the 2022 French proposal, requires the constitution to name Bulgarians (Zhelyazkov, Oct 2025: Sofia adds no new condition to the 2022 proposal). Skopje answers with two conditions (rights for Macedonians in Bulgaria; no further bilateral vetoes) and the Commission notes that no steps have been taken. Incidents keep the wound open: the Ivan Mihailov club sentence (Jun 2025), the arson of two Bulgarian embassy cars in Skopje (15 Jun 2026, suspect detained, motive unknown). The grade is rival, not ally, although both are NATO members (the dataset would derive 'ally'): Sofia's claim that Macedonian language and history are Bulgarian is a contest over identity, and the bilateral friendship treaty of 2017 and Corridor 8 are working in parallel. Trend stable: von der Leyen's visit of 2 Oct 2026 produced a first step, but no movement on the constitution. Bond - grievance: history, language, the 1943 Vatasha anniversary a day after the arson.

But Athens holds the other veto: it accuses Mickoski and President Siljanovska-Davkova of 'flagrant violation' by using 'Macedonia' in domestic contexts, says it will not ratify three cooperation memoranda until Skopje complies, and the government spokesman again tied the EU road to Greece in early October 2026. MNE.note: Mirrors Serbia's own stance toward Montenegro (SRB: rival, kin; Boll Belgrade, 28 May 2026: Montenegro an 'alienated part of Serbian space', a 'doctrine of limited sovereignty'; 2023 census 32.93% Serbs). Seen from Podgorica: Vucic's 14 May 2026 'secession' remarks drew a Foreign Ministry reply that Montenegro 'neither seceded from Serbia nor was ever part of it'; in early June 2026 police banned 87 men flown from Belgrade before the Tivat summit and called it 'hybrid activity'; in August Spajic spoke of coordinated hybrid action by two regional states (media read it as Albania and Serbia, a reading the government itself walked back for Albania). Not 'adversary': Serbia recognised Montenegro within days of the 2006 referendum, is its largest trade partner (17% of imports, 27% of exports) and the largest tourist market, and the government keeps a language of good neighbourliness. Cooling because 2026 added three public clashes to an unresolved dual-citizenship and language agenda. Bond - kin: a third of Montenegro's own citizens declare as Serbs and the Serbian Orthodox Church is the only canonical Orthodox church there (as in Serbia's own stance note); the grade is our structural reading of competing interests, supported by the Boll essay and the 2026 exchanges.

MNE.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded partner - the EU gives candidates no guarantee; ally is reserved for members (Art. 42(7)). Not a treaty ally in the Article 42(7) sense (Montenegro is a candidate), but a stable de facto alignment that the ontology's 'ally' grade covers: 'full and resolute' CFSP alignment praised by the European Parliament on 17 Jun 2026, euro in use since 2002, 18 of 33 chapters provisionally closed by 14 Jul 2026, EU leaders' summit in Tivat on 5 Jun 2026 where von der Leyen called accession 'within reach'. Warming because of the pace of closures and the Growth Plan (EUR 89.3m released by May 2026); the Croatian veto, the Mladic condolences and the UAE procurement exemption are frictions inside the alignment, not changes in structure. Bond - affinity: a stated strategic goal, not kinship.

Bond - affinity: membership is the keystone of the state's post-2006 identity.

MNE.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded reluctant_ally - co-members of NATO/EU with visible friction are allies by necessity, not rivals (ONTOLOGY scale). NATO and EU-candidacy partner on paper, but Croatia is the one EU member that holds a veto on the last chapters and is using it: persona non grata for Speaker Mandic, MP Knezevic and Deputy PM Becic (July 2024, after the Jasenovac resolution); Chapter 31 blocked since December 2024, Chapter 14 and others held on 22 Sep 2026 and the 22 Sep intergovernmental conference cancelled; the 22 Jul 2026 list of demands (Morinj camp compensation, 14 missing, the ship Jadran, maritime border, a swimming-pool name); 'unacceptable' on Mandic's Mladic condolences. Co-membership of NATO would derive an 'ally' stance; the hand-written grade replaces it because on the one objective that matters most (EU entry) Zagreb is the principal obstacle. 'Rival', not 'adversary': Croatia wants the issues settled, not Montenegro defeated. Bond - grievance: the 1991-92 Morinj camp, the Prevlaka and Jadran disputes, and the 2024 Jasenovac resolution.

MNE.note: Montenegro has applied EU sanctions since March 2022, expelled six Russian diplomats on 29 Sep 2022 (Russia then suspended consular services), pledged in November 2025 to tighten visas for Russians, and on 9 Oct 2026 arrested and expelled the founder of the Rybar network with four associates on national-security grounds. The European Parliament (June 2026) names third-country interference and disinformation against Montenegro's EU and NATO course. Not 'adversary': Russia was the first Security Council member to recognise Montenegro in 2006, Russians are 16.4% of foreign overnights (2025) and the state seeks no regime change in Moscow. Bond - grievance: the 2016 coup plot (2019 verdict; 2024 retrial acquitted all defendants, so the judicial record is contested) and Moscow's opposition to NATO accession.

MNE.note: NATO co-member, supports Montenegro's EU path, home of the shared Albanian minority in Ulcinj; Foreign Minister Hoxha called Montenegro 'a friendly NATO ally' in August 2026 when rejecting Spajic's destabilisation claim, and Montenegro told Rama that Albania was not one of the two states meant. Friction is local (the Ulcinj beach lease sparked Albanian protests in April 2025) and episodic, not structural. Belgrade reads Tirana as its greatest threat; Podgorica does not, hence the asymmetric pair with SRB-ALB. Bond - affinity: the Albanian minority and Ulcinj, not kinship of the state.

MNE.note: A friendly neighbour with no alliance: President Milatovic in Sarajevo (2024) called good-neighbourly cooperation an 'imperative' of Montenegro's foreign policy, and the Bosniak Party sits in the governing majority. Frictions come from Republika Srpska: Bosnia protested in February 2024 when RS insignia appeared at a Mandic-Dodik meeting, and Spajic declined to co-sponsor the 2024 UN Srebrenica resolution (voting stance unconfirmed), amending the text instead. The grade rests on 2024 evidence (confidence C); no 2026 bilateral reporting was found. Bond - affinity: a Bosniak community in Montenegro and shared Yugoslav past.

Belgrade's own framing of Montenegro as a Serbian space (Boll, 2026) is the structural backdrop. NLD.note: Treaty ally (NATO, bilateral nuclear sharing, F-35) and the power with which, in the Jetten coalition's words, the Netherlands shares most interests - but aligned by necessity with visible friction: Trump's Greenland tariffs on the Dutch contingent in January 2026 (called 'blackmail' by the caretaker foreign minister, withdrawn on 21 Jan), the Netherlands' refusal of Curaçao for the Venezuela operation and halt to joint counter-drug missions (Jan 2026), Jetten's 'not supported, but understood' reading of the US-Israeli attack on Iran (Mar 2026), the pressure over ASML (MATCH Act) and the 13 Apr 2026 White House dinner that 'did not convince each other'. Rutte, a Dutchman, runs NATO and the Hague summit gave Trump his 5%. Cooling, because every 2026 file has added a friction. Bond - affinity: wartime liberation, the oldest unbroken diplomatic relation (1782).

NLD.note: The deepest integration of any pair in the atlas: the 1 German-Netherlands Corps (since 1995, Münster), all three Dutch combat brigades attached to German divisions (11 Airmobile to the Rapid Forces Division in 2014, 43 Mechanised to the 1st Panzer Division in 2016, 13 Light to the 10th Panzer Division on 30 Mar 2023), a shared tank battalion, and defence industries linked through North Rhine-Westphalia. Merz said in March 2026 that the German armed forces are not so closely interlocked with any other country. Germany is also the Netherlands' first trading partner (about 22% of goods exports). Friction is small and about money (net-contributor camp, EU budget), not about structure. The DEU card holds no row toward NLD, so this is the first side written. Bond - affinity.

NLD.note: Review 2026-10-12: regraded from partner to ally for consistency with the other EU cards: a ten-year bilateral security agreement, F-16s, Patriots and about EUR 20bn of aid are read as a stable de facto alignment (Denmark, Estonia, Italy, Spain), not a partnership. Not an ally: no defence guarantee, but a ten-year bilateral security agreement (2024), F-16s delivered, about EUR 9.1bn spent and EUR 11.6bn earmarked for military support (Dutch figures, July 2026), EUR 1bn into the US-weapons scheme PURL, and a seat in the ten-nation air-defence initiative with Ukraine. Stable and not warming because on 7 Jul 2026 the defence minister said Dutch capacity for new direct aid (Patriot missiles above all) is exhausted. The Netherlands has been a plaintiff with Ukraine against Russia at the ECtHR (9 Jul 2025). Bond - affinity: MH17 and 196 Dutch victims.

NLD.note: A rival with a wound, not a mortal enemy in the ontology's sense: The Hague wants Russia's behaviour changed, sanctioned and judged, not its regime removed. The grievance is MH17: 196 Dutch nationals died on 17 Jul 2014; the ICAO Council (12 May 2025) and the European Court of Human Rights (9 Jul 2025, unanimous) held Russia responsible, and Moscow rejects both. The Hague summit declaration names Russia the main long-term threat, Rotterdam screens sanctioned ships and the government is writing laws against shadow-fleet tankers. If the RUS card grades the Netherlands 'adversary', the pair is asymmetric on purpose. Bond - grievance.

NLD.note: The key China episode is Nexperia: the Dutch state took control of the Chinese-owned chipmaker on 12 Oct 2025 (Goods Availability Act), Beijing banned the export of Nexperia China's chips from 4 Oct, European carmakers neared a stop, and The Hague suspended its order on 19 Nov 2025; litigation, a Chinese court freeze of about USD 300m (31 Aug 2026) and a split Nexperia continue. Since then the two have worked a 'pragmatic reset': Berendsen-Wang Yi call (13 Mar 2026, 'one of the most important bilateral relationships'), the first ministerial trade mission since 2018 (Sjoerdsma, July 2026). Meanwhile ASML's export controls (since 2023, under American pressure) cut China out of the most advanced machines. China is a trading partner worth about EUR 90bn a year (2024), so cooperation out of necessity while resisting alignment. No source calls it 'reluctant partner'; the grade is our reading (C). Bond - none.

NLD.note: Still a partner in trade, security and intelligence, but cooling fast and visibly: entry ban on Ben-Gvir and Smotrich (28 Jul 2025), foreign minister Veldkamp's resignation (22 Aug 2025) and the NSC's exit when the cabinet would not go further, the Dutch push with Sweden for EU sanctions and suspension of the trade part of the Association Agreement (Aug 2025), the Jetten coalition's 'sanctions against the Netanyahu government stay until meaningful steps', a ban on settlement goods in force from 22 Sep 2026, and Israel's withdrawal of the status of the Dutch diplomats in Ramallah (27 Sep). The Hague insists the measures are 'not directed at Israel' and still wants Hamas disarmed and Israel secure. Kept at partner and not rival because no source speaks of competing interests, only of conditions; the grade is our reading (C). Bond - affinity (history, Holocaust memory).

NLD.note: No posture of its own, but the Kingdom's islands are Venezuela's immediate neighbours: the Netherlands kept out of the US build-up (Aug 2025) and of the 3 Jan 2026 operation that seized Maduro, said it was 'shocked' but 'did not shed tears', refused the use of Curaçao and keeps Dutch equipment on notice to move in the Caribbean; the military intelligence service (April 2026) described the US build-up as seen by Caracas as an intervention threat. NLD.note: Founding member (1958), Article 42(7) applies. A frugal member rather than a federalist one: with Germany, Austria, Denmark, Finland and Sweden it asked on 28 Sep 2026 for cuts of several hundred billion euros in the 2028-34 budget; no eurobonds but support for SAFE and a Defence Fund; backed the EU-Mercosur deal in Nov 2025 after long reluctance (farmers still opposed); and in Sept 2024 asked Brussels for an asylum opt-out, which the Commission said was impossible without a treaty change. The Jetten coalition returns to the pro-European mainstream (a European sanctions authority, a Defence Mechanism). Bond - affinity.

NLD.note: Constituent country of the Kingdom since its separate status (status aparte) on 1 Jan 1986; foreign relations and defence are Kingdom affairs under the Charter, and Dutch embassies represent all four countries. Local autonomy is wide (education, judiciary, health, tourism). Aruba lies close to the Venezuelan coast and shares with Curaçao a US Forward Operating Location for counter-drug flights; since January 2026 the Netherlands has halted joint counter-drug operations with the US and keeps its own units on notice. Own territory, but not one the Hague can dispose of alone (changes to the Charter need all four countries). Bond - kin.

Own territory, but with a local government whose consent the Charter requires for changes. Bond - kin.

'Rival', not 'adversary': Norway states no aim against Russia's regime, keeps the 1976 fisheries regime (2026 quotas agreed Dec 2025) and the Svalbard Treaty framework working, and Tromsø, Båtsfjord and Kirkenes stay partly open to Russian fishing vessels. No source uses the word 'rival'; the grade is our reading (confidence B). Bond - none: the liberation of Finnmark in 1944 is a memory of both, not a tie.

org-nato.note: Rival, not adversary, in the ontology's terms. The 2022 Strategic Concept names Russia 'the most significant and direct threat' and the Ankara declaration (8 Jul 2026) 'the long-term threat', Eastern Sentry (12 Sep 2025), Baltic Sentry (Jan 2025) and two Article 4 sessions in September 2025 (Poland, Estonia) show the contest; NATO suspended practical cooperation in April 2014 and expelled eight Russian officials in October 2021, after which Moscow closed its mission. But NATO's declared aim is deterrence and defence, not the end of the Russian state or regime, and the channel for dialogue is kept formally open; Peskov himself said Moscow stays open to dialogue when there is a chance for constructive engagement. A threat label in an official text is the source for the hostile reading, the grade follows the structure (a standing deterrence contest, no allied war aim against Russia). Trend cooling: airspace violations (Estonia MiG-31s, 19 Sep 2025) and Russian drones in Poland rose in 2025-26. Bond - grievance: Moscow's reading of enlargement as encirclement, and NATO's of 2014 and 2022 as betrayal.

NATO runs NSATU (Wiesbaden, operating since December 2024) and the PURL scheme (about USD 6.7bn of US weapons paid by allies in a year). Stable: more money and more words, no door. org-nato.note: The member that is also the question. Structurally the United States is the guarantor and the founder (Article 5, the nuclear umbrella, about 80,000 troops in Europe, 57% of alliance spending), so this is an alliance and not a rivalry; the grade is reluctant_ally because the alignment is held by necessity under visible friction: the Pentagon's 'NATO 3.0' (Colby, Feb 2026), the cut to the Force Model (May-June 2026), 5,000 troops leaving Germany (announced 1 May 2026) and a posture review weighing 25,000-40,000 withdrawals, Trump's 'NATO WASN'T THERE WHEN WE NEEDED THEM' over the Iran war, doubts about Article 5 before Ankara and the Greenland coercion of Denmark (settled on paper on 22 Sep 2026). Counter-signals keep it from rival: Trump signed the 'ironclad' Article 5 at Ankara and the US still supplies the PURL stocks and the nuclear deterrent. No source applies the word 'reluctant' to NATO's side: our reading (confidence C), consistent with how DNK, GBR and NLD are graded toward the USA. Cooling since 2025. Bond - affinity: 77 years of shared institution.

So not an adversary. Rival because allied territory is part of the contest - Romania, Italy, Germany, Britain, Portugal, Greece and others implemented US basing requests, Spain refused - and Iran accused the Alliance of complicity in June 2026 and named Romania and Italy. org-nato.note: Partner, the grade for the EU toward non-members of its structure: 23 of the 27 EU states are allies, the Strategic Concept calls the EU a 'unique and essential partner', and the third joint declaration (10 Jan 2023) holds that a stronger European defence is 'complementary to, and interoperable with NATO'. Warming because in July 2026 Rutte and von der Leyen jointly called for a 'more European NATO' with a clear division of labour (NATO command, capabilities and standards; EU industry, investment and regulation), Merz made the same case in Ankara, and Rutte argued for Turkey's inclusion in EU defence schemes (SAFE). The duplication question (Albright's 'no duplication' of 1998) is the standing friction: SAFE loans are limited to EU states and exclude non-EU allies such as Turkey, the UK and Canada unless agreed. Not an ally: the EU holds no Article 5; Article 42(7) is separate. Bond - affinity: shared membership, not kinship.

PAK.note: The ontology test for 'adversary' is a declared aim of the other's destruction or regime change, and it fails on both sides. Pakistan's aim is deterrence, Kashmir and water: the defence minister and the PM threaten force only if India attacks again or diverts the Indus ('act of war', UN, Sept 2026); the May 2025 war was four days of limited strikes ended by a ceasefire (10 May) through the military hotline, and Track-2 meetings in Muscat, Doha and London are reported. India's own measures (Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance since 23 Apr 2025, trade and visas suspended) are coercion, not a bid to end the Pakistani state. Everything else is rivalry at its sharpest: nuclear-armed, no official dialogue, an arms race (Fatah-IV, Rocket Force) and a water lever that Pakistan calls an existential threat. If India diverts flow or strikes the leadership, the grade should be reopened. Bond - grievance: partition, four wars and Kashmir.

PAK.note: The hardest edge case in the atlas. PSE.note: Decided from the evidence: rival, not adversary. The PLO accepts Israel and the two-state outcome (Abbas to the UN, 24 Sep 2026: a two-state solution on international law) and the PA still lives inside the Oslo security and customs architecture, so it does not seek Israel's destruction; the coordination it has never fully ended (Arab Center: dense, and kept going through earlier suspensions) is the opposite of an adversary's posture. The hostility is real and one-sided in intent: the occupation (ICJ 2024: unlawful), the withholding of clearance revenues since May 2025, the E1 tenders of Aug 2026, the first Area A land seizure for settlements, settler violence at record levels (UN: about 1,430 incidents to 10 Aug 2026), and, per PISM, a coalition aim of blocking statehood and, if the far right wins, dismantling the PA. Israel's own grade of the PA may be harsher (build will flag the asymmetry if Jerusalem's card says adversary). No source uses the word 'rival': the grade is our reading of the structure (confidence C). Cooling: the Israeli election of 27 Oct 2026 is contested by blocs most of which oppose a Palestinian state (Al Jazeera). Bond - grievance: occupation, 1948 and 1967.

QAT.note: The grade rests on three official facts. Executive Order 14353 (29 Sep 2025) makes any armed attack on Qatar's territory, sovereignty or critical infrastructure a threat to the peace and security of the United States, with joint contingency planning and diplomatic, economic and, if necessary, military response; Qatar was designated a major non-NATO ally on 10 Mar 2022; and Al Udeid, the largest US base in the region (about 10,000 personnel), sits on its soil. Qatar buys the alliance with money: USD 243.5bn of announced deals during Trump's visit of May 2025 (arms of about USD 3bn), a Qatari Air Force facility at Mountain Home (Oct 2025), emergency-fast-tracked Patriot and APKWS replenishment (May 2026), a gifted 747 for Air Force One. It is `ally` rather than `reluctant_ally` because Doha chose and pays for the arrangement; the friction is real but does not change the structure: a US partner struck its capital on 9 Sep 2025 with Washington on notice, the order is an executive act, not a Senate treaty, and Qatar's spokesman now says the US alliance is 'important but insufficient' and that security self-sufficiency is 'the only way forward' while it deepens ties with Turkey and Pakistan. Bond none: interest, not kinship.

Qatar expelled Iran's military and security attaches on 18-19 Mar, summoned the deputy ambassador in July, and then sent its prime minister to Tehran on 27 Aug 2026 to discuss a Hormuz shipping corridor and joint demining; it keeps relaying US-Iran messages (foreign ministry briefing of 6 Oct 2026) and sent a delegation to Khamenei's funeral. `reluctant_partner` because it cooperates out of necessity (Hormuz carries about 93% of its LNG, the field is shared) while resisting Iranian coercion; not `rival` because Doha seeks de-escalation and not Iran's defeat, not `adversary` for the same reason. Qatar declined in March to lead the mediation 'so that attacking Qatar does not earn Iran better terms', then returned to it by August. Bond none.

UKR.note: The only mortal-enemy grade in Ukraine's map, and the structural one: Russia's aim, as ISW reads the Kremlin's position in February 2026, is neutrality, a limited army and a pro-Russian government in Kyiv; the Atlantic Council argues that Putin cannot accept any deal that secures Ukrainian statehood. Kyiv's reading is on the record: the Rada asked the US to name Russia a state sponsor of terrorism (May 2022) and PACE declared the Russian regime terrorist (Oct 2022). Since January 2026 the two have talked (Abu Dhabi, Geneva, with the US) and the Kremlin has insisted on the Donbas, so 'adversary' is not rhetoric; it describes a war whose settlement would decide whether Ukraine remains a state. Bond - grievance: the open wound is 2014 and 2022, not kinship, whatever Putin says about 'one people'.
